summary:
Two engineering-prepared client documents (both dated 2026-07-04) from /Users/harshahirrao/Speed gym/docs/reference/: VMSG_CLIENT_BRIEF.md (project brief) and VMSG_CONTENT_READINESS.md (content audit). The brief describes Vedic Math Speed Gym as an offline-first mobile (Android + iOS) and web app training Vedic mathematics and exam prep (CAT/GMAT/GRE). It observes how each learner makes mistakes, drills exact weaknesses, wraps practice in competitive games, and works fully offline. Monetization: free users get manual topic practice with ads; paid users get the "Decision Engine" (a smart session planner/personal coach). Architecture has five layers: the on-device app (runs practice, games, scoring locally), the Decision Engine "brain", a live-multiplayer game server ("referee"), two databases (one for facts/history, one for the topic-connection "map" — i.e., a graph DB), and an overnight "content factory" that generates and verifies problems (never touches the live game; AI never invents a problem on the fly — everything is pre-verified). The build is against an RFP v7.2 with 365 specifications, judged solid. Plan: Phase 1 = 15 weeks to build everything (accounts/QR login/payments with Stripe + Razorpay, family plans, learning engine with mastery tracking and the 16 Vedic techniques, head-to-head duels with matchmaking, content + hints-only study chatbot tutor, admin panel, social features — streaks, referrals, achievements, leaderboards, basic team play — mock exams, app-store submission, closed beta with 100+ testers). Advanced team games (Boss Battles, Relay, Tournaments, location features) are built in Phase 1 but kept switched off. Phase 2 = 6 weeks (weeks 16–21), triggered at 5,000 daily users: provision larger infra, zero-downtime data and service migration, load-test at 10,000 req/s, switch on Boss Battles/Tournaments/advanced analytics/smart models, then monitoring and handover. Infra cost: Phase 1 ~2 small servers ($80–120/mo), optional middle step ~6 servers (~$108/mo), Phase 2 22 servers (~$836/mo); ad revenue expected to cover Phase-1 running cost. Five discussion points for the client: (1) keep the 15-week date by reusing already-prepared content and shipping advanced models dormant; (2) "smart but silent" — advanced scoring models for reading and logical-reasoning sections run in the background collecting calibration data and only go live in Phase 2 once accurate (they need thousands of users); (3) never sample the practice-attempt data the learning engine needs — sample only non-essential telemetry (page views, help clicks); (4) AI bot opponents fill empty lobbies for adults but must never be shown to kids' (COPPA) accounts, with a terms-of-service disclosure; (5) optional infra middle step. Open confirmations needed: content ownership, primary payment region (Stripe vs Razorpay affects default currency), and whether narrator voice-over is in Phase 1. Eight go/no-go launch gates: code quality, security scan, speed under load, device coverage, accessibility, integration testing, stable real-user beta, and the 5,000-DAU Phase-2 trigger.

The content-readiness report audits the delivered content package `topic_browser_full_package` (dated 2026-06-19) and gives a green light: the practice engine can be built on this content today. Library counts: 807 practice problems, 791 step-by-step walkthroughs, 590 concept explainers, 908 common-mistake traps (tagged error patterns), 467 skills tracked, 16 Vedic sutras, ~1,505 problem templates (generate near-unlimited verified variations), 4,943 source passages extracted from source books — roughly 2,200 ready practice pieces plus templates. Health: only 3 of 807 questions missing text; 789/807 (97.8%) machine-verified correct by an automated math checker; prerequisite map complete with 2,457 links; ~1,570 common-mistake tags; 18 questions missing an answer key (16 missing key + 2 flagged for review) — a quick first-sprint batch fix. Important correction: earlier planning documents claiming "240 questions with missing text", "only 15 prerequisite links", and a "63.7% failure" rate are out of date; the 63.7% figure comes from a stale `problems.jsonl` export predating re-verification and should simply be regenerated from current verified data. The one client decision: the Reference Library has 28 per-technique pages (formula, when to use, worked example, top traps) of which only 3 are written and approved and 25 are "coming soon"; options are A) auto-draft + human review (recommended, fastest), B) fully human-written (highest quality, slower), C) launch with 3 and add later (zero delay). This choice does not affect the practice engine, games, or personalization.

workstream_notes.backend: The brief fixes the backend shape: on-device scoring (offline-first — nothing answering a math problem touches the network), a Decision Engine service, a separate real-time game server for multiplayer duels, and two databases (relational facts/history + a graph-style topic map with 2,457 prerequisite links). Phase 1 targets 2 small servers ($80-120/mo) scaling to 22 at 5,000 DAU ($836/mo), with an optional ~6-server middle step; Phase 2 must survive 10,000 req/s load tests. Backend must support accounts, QR login, Stripe + Razorpay subscriptions, family plans/child seats, COPPA kids' mode, AI lobby bots gated off for child accounts, and 100% retention of practice-attempt events (sampling allowed only for non-essential telemetry). Advanced models (reading/LR scoring) ship dormant, collecting calibration data, toggled live in Phase 2 via feature flags — build flag infrastructure accordingly. 8 launch gates including security scan and accessibility.
workstream_notes.data_extraction: The extraction pipeline has already produced 4,943 source passages from the source books inside topic_browser_full_package (2026-06-19). Known data-quality state to build on: 3 questions with missing text (out of 807), 18 missing answer keys (16 no key + 2 flagged), ~1,570 mistake tags applied, 97.8% of problems machine-verified. Critical: ignore legacy figures (240 missing-text, 15 prereq links, 63.7% failure) — they come from a stale problems.jsonl that must be regenerated from the current verified data. A 'content pre-flight check' is scheduled for weeks 1-2 of the build.
workstream_notes.rag: The 'content factory' is the RAG/content workstream: it runs overnight, generates problems from ~1,505 templates, and every item is machine-verified before it can appear in the app — AI never generates a problem live during play. Current corpus: 807 problems, 791 walkthroughs, 590 explainers, 908 mistake traps, 467 skills, 16 sutras, 4,943 source passages — already sufficient for launch. The one open generation task: 25 of 28 Reference Library pages are unwritten; recommended path is auto-draft by the system + human review (option A), which the content factory would produce during the build. Also planned: a hints-only study chatbot tutor (weeks 9-10), which is a RAG-adjacent feature over the lesson/content corpus.
